name: Accenting — A Little Extra Where It Matters Most
summary: Pleasure isn't symmetrical. Giving extra attention to specific spots—rather than treating everything equally—intensifies sensation, like pressing harder on a knot during a back massage. Accent one part of any motion to hit the receiver's offset hotspot.
detailed_description: The visible clitoris is the tip of an iceberg of surrounding tissue, and the most intense spot is often offset rather than dead center—top-right, top-left, left side, and so on. OMGYES reports about 1 in 8 women prefer extra attention on one specific side. Accenting means taking any working motion and making one part of it more intense: harder pressure, deeper push, or a faster sweep in one direction as you cross the preferred spot. Clock-face language ('I'm a 3 o'clock person') or directional terms help communicate the location.
stepwise_structure: 1. Wait until the warmup stage—accent when the clit is awake and responsive.
2. Start from a motion both partners already enjoy.

3. Accent just one part of the motion: e.g. press harder on the downstroke only when crossing the hotspot side, push deeper at a preferred corner on a side-to-side, or sweep faster toward one direction and gentler on the return.
4. Repeat the accented motion consistently—buildup needs repetition.
5. To find the hotspot, test locations systematically (top-right, top-left, left side, etc.), at least 10 repetitions each before dismissing one.
6. Use clock-face or directional language to name the spot.
safety_notes: Don't accent motions that hurt, especially when moving upward onto unprotected tissue.
Favorite spots change day to day—keep experimenting rather than assuming.
Adults in consensual contexts only; not a substitute for professional care.
